title: Permission Cost Nudges: Inline RBAC Guidance + Cost Attribution in Console
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Problem: Teams routinely grant broad workspace permissions (Admin/Editor) to enable fast setup. That often increases inference spend and makes cost attribution noisy. PMs and finance want clearer signals in the Console to guide safer, cost-aware permission choices. Goal: Design an inline UX inside the workspace Role Editor and the Deployments dashboard that surfaces estimated monthly cost impact when granting or changing role scopes, suggest least-privilege templates with cost delta, and provide a lightweight audit snapshot for recent changes. We will prototype both an editor nudge and a dashboard cost-overlay, then run moderated usability tests and an internal A/B rollout to Platform customers. User stories: 1) As a workspace admin, I want to see if granting 'Model Deploy' scope to a token will materially increase monthly spend before saving. 2) As a platform owner, I want suggested role templates that balance developer productivity and cost containment. 3) As a finance reviewer, I want a concise audit snapshot showing which role changes caused cost deltas in the last 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: Inline Role Editor shows a clear, non-blocking 'Estimated cost delta' badge when any permission affecting inference usage is toggled.
Role suggestion drawer surfaces at least three template roles (Least-Privilege, Balanced, Broad) with approximate monthly cost ranges and short rationale.
Cost overlay can be toggled on the Deployments dashboard to highlight top 5 roles/tokens by attributed inference spend.
Prototype usability test (n=6 internal + 6 external early users) with SUS >= 75 or qualitative agreement that nudges are helpful, not noisy.
Design handoff artifacts include Figma frames, an annotated interaction spec, and a small set of metrics for the rollout (click-through, role-change conversion, cost delta tracked).
decisions: Use non-blocking informational nudges rather than permission enforcement to avoid blocking operational workflows.
Estimate granularity: show monthly ranges (Low / Medium / High) derived from 90th-percentile per-token cost model rather than per-request exacts to avoid false precision.
Expose a toggle for operators to turn off cost nudges at the org level (respecting private deployment requirements).
feedback: PM review (Rohit Patel): Align language with billing terms; replace 'cost' with 'estimated spend' in copy for legal clarity.
Eng review (Maya Kim): Backend needs a lightweight cost projection endpoint; can reuse sampled token distributions from Optimize pipeline.
Security review request: Ensure no new permissions are implied by the feature; add opt-out for audited orgs (requested by Security).
Design critique (Weekly UX): Reduce visual weight of badge; preferred thin outline with hover tooltip and link to 'why this matters' modal.

notes: This ticket intentionally pairs console UX with cost signals — different from prior audit-led prototypes that focused on replay and temporal grants.
We will iterate copy to avoid blame; primary message: 'Understand impact' not 'restrict access'.
Consider integrating with Optimize recommendations in a later phase (follow-up ticket).
usability_findings: Participants expected the estimate to be conservative; when numbers were high they wanted a 'how is this calculated' link.
Some admins feared the nudge would be visible to developers and lead to confusion; we recommend scoping visibility to admins and role editors by default.
Balanced template was the most selected in tests (8/12) when paired with short explanation of trade-offs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha — show nudges to Platform and Design (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Beta rollout to 10 enterprise orgs behind feature flag, collect metrics (4 weeks).
Phase 3: Gradual ramp with A/B test measuring role-change conversion and attributed inference spend over 3 months.
metrics: Role-change conversion rate (save after opening editor)
Delta in average inference spend per workspace after role change (30d)
